The third case is a study in demography. The original authors (OAs) compared the first cohabitations of American women begun in the early 1990s with those begun in the late 2000s, from two surveys of the National Survey of Family Growth (NSFG), and asked how often the couples went on to marry. A union observed for a few months and one observed for five years cannot be compared by whether they had married by the interview, so the case needs the methods of event-history analysis: censoring, the life table, and data with one row for every month in which a union could end. This week covers the data and those first methods. Read only sections 1 to 3 of the case study this week. Leave its later sections, and the menu, the decision map, the multiverse page and the cheatsheet of the case, until after Task 3 next week, which asks you to find out for yourself what those pages describe.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| The paper of the OAs [@KuoRaley2016DivergingPatternsUnion] | Before class. Read the whole article: the retreat from marriage that it addresses, the two surveys and the unions of the two cohorts, the life table, the models of Table 2 fitted to person-months, the main finding by education, and the sentence of the conclusions from which SCORE took the claim. | 75 minutes |
| [Case study](../../cases/cohabitation/index.qmd), sections 1 to 3 | Before class. [The original study](../../cases/cohabitation/index.qmd#sec-study), its data and its model; [SCORE and Multi100](../../cases/cohabitation/index.qmd#sec-score) and the claim as Multi100 recorded it; and [the five reanalyses](../../cases/cohabitation/index.qmd#sec-reanalysts), which reached three different conclusions from one file. | 40 minutes |
| [Codebook of the union file](../../cases/cohabitation/data/cohab_unions_codebook.md) and [the claim](../../cases/cohabitation/exercise.qmd#the-claim) on the exercise overview | The source of the unions in five surveys of the NSFG, which are in the public domain, the data use restrictions of the National Center for Health Statistics that still bind them, the unions of each survey, and how the start and the end of a union are found. Then the claim and the published coefficient behind it. | 25 minutes |
| [Setup](../../setup.qmd#the-workspace) | Before class, Task 1 of the case. Download the workspace of the cohabitation case and run `source("R/check_setup.R")` until it prints OK; the last check fits the reference specification of the course and prints −0.730. Everything that the case needs, the file of Task 3 included, is already in the `data/` folder of the workspace. | 20 minutes |
| Slides, Part 2 | In class. The paper of the OAs, with its life table, its model on person-months and the claim as SCORE selected it; a table of what the five analysts compared and reported; and the claim: the estimand statement that the class writes and sends together, who cohabits in each cohort, and selection into cohabitation as conditioning on a collider. The estimands run and the causal-graph crash course repeat week 3, so the class passes over them. | 40 minutes |
| Task 2 in your report or working script, or [Browser lab](../../cases/cohabitation/lab.qmd#task-2-data) Task 2 | In class. Count the unions of each survey and the 929 and 1,142 unions of the paper with their outcomes; compute the weighted shares of Hispanic, Black and white women among the cohabitors of each cohort; turn the unions into person-months with `spec_frame(unions)` and draw the life table. Write the [estimand statement](../../cases/cohabitation/lab.qmd#task-2-estimand-and-graph), saying which cohorts and what you hold constant, then open `R/dag_starter.R`, keep the arrows that you are willing to defend, run `adjustmentSets(dag)` and the two calls of `paths()` that the file holds, and add the arrow from the period to the age at the start. | 35 minutes |
| [Event-history analysis](../../companion/event-history.qmd), sections 1 and 2 | [Time to an event and censoring](../../companion/event-history.qmd#sec-time), and why the share married by the interview mixes the event with the time that each union was observed; then [the life table](../../companion/event-history.qmd#sec-lifetable), the hazard, and marriage and separation as competing events. The later sections of the module come next week. | 65 minutes |

**By the end of the session** you have the workspace of the case passing its setup check, the unions of the paper counted and turned into person-months, the life table of the two cohorts drawn, the estimand behind the claim written in one sentence, and two sentences on what keeping only women who cohabited does to a comparison of two periods.
